# `fluxsim replay`

Re-execute a recorded plan and refuse unless the run digest it produces is the one asserted. The determinism claim, as a command.

## Synopsis

```text
fluxsim replay [options] <bundle>
```

## Examples

```bash
# re-execute the plan; refuse unless the run digest is the one asserted
fluxsim replay ./bundle --run-id de72fa4b22711c52 \
    --assert-digest sha256:42d923fd6f4b8c0a1e7d59b2c8a4f36e0d15927acb3e8f6410d2b7c95e8a3f01
```

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `bundle` | path to the FLUX bundle directory |

## Options

| Option | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--run-id` | `RUN_ID` | the run id to act on (as reported by `fluxsim plan`/`fluxsim run`) **(required)** |
| `--assert-digest` | `sha256:HEX` | the runDigest this replay must reproduce, as sha256:&lt;64 hex chars&gt;; the bare hex is accepted and the prefix put back **(required)** |
| `--simulation-id` | `SIMULATION_ID` | which Simulation document to resolve (default: the bundle's only one) |
| `--zone` | `ZONE` | declared run zone, for sovereignty checks |
| `--state-dir` | `STATE_DIR` | run-state directory (default: ./.flux) |
| `-j, --json` |  | emit machine-readable JSON |
